bank.prompt: Fortitude Valley got its name from a ship that arrived in Brisbane in 1849. What was that ship called?
bank.reveal: Scottish immigrants aboard the barque Fortitude arrived at Brisbane in January 1849. Denied promised free land, they camped nearby — and named the area after their ship.

source.title: Fortitude Valley | Queensland Places
source.publisher: Centre for the Government of Queensland
source.verifierNote: Page states 'The first vessel, the Fortitude, arrived at Brisbane in January 1849' and 'The temporary abode gave rise to the name Fortitude Valley.'

bank.prompt: The suburb name 'Indooroopilly' comes from an Aboriginal word. What does it mean?
bank.reveal: Brisbane City Council's Heritage Trail explains the name comes from an Aboriginal word believed to mean a gully or creek with leeches — a nod to the leech-filled gullies once running to the Brisbane River.

source.title: Indooroopilly Heritage Trail | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states 'The name Indooroopilly is thought to come from an Aboriginal word. It is believed to mean a gully or creek with leeches.'

bank.prompt: Brisbane City Hall's famous pipe organ was NOT built for City Hall. Where was it originally installed when it arrived in Brisbane in 1892?

options.label: The Brisbane Exhibition Building, Bowen Park
St John's Anglican Cathedral, Ann Street

bank.reveal: Built by Henry Willis & Sons in 1891–92, the organ first lived at the Exhibition Building in Bowen Park for 35 years before being moved and enlarged for City Hall in 1927.

source.title: Brisbane City Hall – Pierce Pipe Organs
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'This instrument was originally built by Henry Willis and Sons in England between 1891-2 and first erected in the Brisbane Exhibition Hall, Bowen Park.'

bank.prompt: Brisbane's Story Bridge wasn't always called the Story Bridge. What was it officially known as during construction from 1935?
bank.reveal: Named to honour King George V's Silver Jubilee, it was renamed Story Bridge at its 1940 opening after JD Story, Public Service Commissioner — the King had died in 1936.

source.title: Story Bridge | Environment, land and water | Queensland Government
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'From mid-1935 to 1940 the bridge was known as the Jubilee Bridge, honouring George V, but when opened on 6 July 1940 it was named after JD Story, the Public Service Commissioner and a member of the Bridge Board.'

bank.prompt: Which came first: the opening of the William Jolly Bridge or the opening of the Story Bridge?
bank.reveal: The William Jolly Bridge (then called Grey Street Bridge) opened 30 March 1932 — nearly eight years before the Story Bridge opened on 6 July 1940.

source.title: William Jolly Bridge Brisbane | State Library of Queensland
source.verifierNote: Page states the William Jolly Bridge was 'the second one built to cross the Brisbane River, opening on 30 March 1932 and nearly eight years before the Story Bridge'.

bank.prompt: Which opened first at Brisbane's South Bank Cultural Centre: the Queensland Art Gallery building or QPAC?
bank.reveal: The Queensland Art Gallery opened on 21 June 1982 as the first stage of the Cultural Centre. QPAC followed three years later, officially opened on 20 April 1985.

source.title: About – Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art
source.publisher: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA)
source.verifierNote: Official QAGOMA page states QAG 'Opened: 21 June 1982'; QPAC's own official history page (qpac.com.au/corporate/history) states it 'officially opened by His Royal Highness the Duke of Kent on 20 April 1985'.

bank.prompt: In what year did Brisbane's very first horse-drawn tramcar begin passenger service?
bank.reveal: The horse-drawn service started on 10 August 1885; electric trams didn't arrive until 1897, often confused as Brisbane's 'first' trams.

source.title: Tram Pole | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'Construction of the tramway network began in early 1885, and Brisbane's first horse-drawn tramcar operated on 10 August of the same year.' Also states first electric trams arrived in 1897.

bank.prompt: Fernberg — now Queensland's Government House — has been the official home of Queensland Governors since which year?
bank.reveal: Fernberg was built in 1865 by merchant Johann Heussler, but Queensland Governors only moved in from 1910, after the original Government House became the University of Queensland.

source.title: The History | Government House Queensland
source.verifierNote: Page states: ''Fernberg' was one of the first houses built in Brisbane's Paddington area and since 1910, has been the home and workplace of Queensland Governors.' Also references the original merchant-built villa of 1865.

bank.prompt: The Story Bridge is one of Brisbane's most iconic landmarks — but who was it named after?
bank.reveal: It honours J.D. Story, Queensland's Public Service Commissioner 1920–39 — not designer John Bradfield, who built Sydney Harbour Bridge.

source.title: 80 years strong – A Story Bridge Anniversary
source.verifierNote: Page states the bridge 'was named after J.D. Story, a prominent Queensland public servant who held the position of Public Service Commissioner from 1920 up until 1939' — explicitly distinguishing him from engineer Bradfield.

bank.prompt: Brisbane's beloved Ekka is officially the *Royal* Queensland Show — but in what year did it earn the 'Royal' prefix?
bank.reveal: King George V granted the 'Royal' prefix by warrant in 1921, 45 years after the very first Exhibition was held at Bowen Park in 1876.

source.title: About the RNA
source.publisher: Royal National Agricultural and Industrial Association of Queensland (RNA)
source.verifierNote: Page explicitly states: 'The first Royal Show was held in 1921, when the Association was granted the prefix under warrant from His Majesty King George V.'
